evidence.quote:
For every fixed real constant $C>1$, there is a polynomial-time reduction from $3$CNF satisfiability to finite undirected graphs with nonnegative rational capacities and exactly unit demands, together with a positive rational threshold $a$, such that $$\begin{array}{ll}
 \text{the formula is satisfiable}&\Longrightarrow\ \Phi(G)\le a,\\[2pt]
 \text{the formula is unsatisfiable}&\Longrightarrow\ \Phi(G)>Ca.
 \end{array}$$ The graph size and the bit lengths of all output numbers are polynomial in the formula size, with constants and exponents allowed to depend on $C$.

exclusions.query: Polynomial-time constant-factor solver for general Uniform Sparsest Cut
exclusions.reason: The central construction establishes hardness of the approximation search problem; it supplies gap instances rather than an approximation solver.

evidence.quote: The construction is polynomial in the formula size; no claim is made that its exponent is uniform in $C$.

exclusions.query: Uniform polynomial dependence on the approximation factor
exclusions.reason: The factor is fixed first, and the source explicitly permits its value to influence the polynomial exponent.

evidence.quote: A factor-$C$ approximation must return a nonempty proper cut whose ratio is at most $C\Phi(G)$.

exclusions.query: Hardness of evaluating the capacity of a supplied cut
exclusions.reason: The objective and approximation contract concern selecting a cut with a guarantee relative to the minimum. They do not assert hardness of evaluating a specified cut.

evidence.quote: Only the selected pairs carry unit demand; they need not include all distinct vertex pairs.

exclusions.query: Hardness for arbitrary nonuniform demand objectives from this direct reduction
exclusions.reason: The main theorem fixes unit demands on all distinct vertex pairs, while the historical discussion distinguishes selected-pair nonuniform demands.

evidence.quote: ### Finite graphs with exactly uniform demands We now convert Theorem 13 into the graph promised in Theorem 1. The conversion must retain cuts of arbitrarily small positive mass. In particular, replacing the demand by an additive approximation alone would be insufficient. We keep a multiplicative upper bound on the retained demand and attach every remaining vertex to that demand.

We first bound the normalization of the successful event, then expose a common conditional density. Finally, one prefix and one threshold will satisfy every calibration and order requirement simultaneously.

outputs.exact_statement:
For every fixed real constant $C>1$, there is a polynomial-time reduction from $3$CNF satisfiability to finite undirected graphs with nonnegative rational capacities and exactly unit demands, together with a positive rational threshold $a$, such that $$\begin{array}{ll}
 \text{the formula is satisfiable}&\Longrightarrow\ \Phi(G)\le a,\\[2pt]
 \text{the formula is unsatisfiable}&\Longrightarrow\ \Phi(G)>Ca.
 \end{array}$$ The graph size and the bit lengths of all output numbers are polynomial in the formula size, with constants and exponents allowed to depend on $C$. In particular, approximating Uniform Sparsest Cut within any fixed factor $C>1$ is NP-hard.

For every $0<\lambda_0<1$ and every sufficiently large power of two $r$, put $q=r^2$. There is a deterministic algorithm which, given an integer $d\geq 1$, constructs a list $$u_1,\ldots,u_m\in\mathbb F_q^d$$ with the following properties:*

1.  *$m=O(d)$, and the list contains every standard basis vector of $\mathbb F_q^d$;*

2.  *if a homogeneous quadratic polynomial $Q$ in $d$ variables does not vanish at every point of the list, then $$\#\{j:Q(u_j)=0\}\leq\lambda_0m.$$*

*The running time is $2^{O(d)}$ bit operations. The constants in both bounds may depend on $r$, which is fixed independently of $d$.

Let $b\in k((z))$ have order $-1$. The polynomial $X^r+X-b$ is irreducible over $k((z))$. Its extension is a Laurent series field $k((w))$, where $w=1/X$ and $z$ has order $r$ in $w$. Its integral lattice has the basis $$1,w,\ldots,w^{r-1}\quad\text{over }k[[z]],$$ and the discriminant of this basis has $z$-order $2(r-1)$.

For every fixed $\lambda>0$ there are constants $\eta>0$, $B<\infty$, and a fixed finite list of bounded-arity test laws with the following properties. From a Boolean $3$CNF formula one can construct, in polynomial time, a finite uniform space $\mathcal S$ of bit positions and these test laws on $\mathcal S$.* 1. *Every individual question marginal is at most $B$ times uniform measure on $\mathcal S$. All samplers are polynomially enumerable finite weighted lists with rational probabilities; every positive seed probability is at least inverse-polynomial in the input size.* 2. *If the formula is satisfiable, there is an assignment $y:\mathcal S\to\mathbb F_2$ accepted by every test in every support.* 3. *If the formula is unsatisfiable, every assignment fails one of the test laws with probability greater than $\eta$.* 4. *There is also an exchangeable law of $(s_1,s_2,s_3,s_4)\in\mathcal S^4$, with uniform marginals, such that the conditional expectation operator of any coordinate given any other has norm at most $\lambda$ on mean-zero $L^2(\mathcal S)$. The assignment in (ii) satisfies $$y_{s_1}+y_{s_2}+y_{s_3}+y_{s_4}=0 \qquad\text{in }\mathbb F_2$$ throughout the support of this law.* *All constants, including the degrees of the polynomial size and time bounds, depend only on $\lambda$. Two independent copies of the law in (iv), paired coordinatewise, have the same pair-operator bound on $\mathcal S^2$ and give the corresponding parity identity for the expressions $y_i+y_j$.
Every pair-operator of Equation [eq:four-masked-positions] has mean-zero norm at most $$\max\{\lambda_1,\,2/(q-3)\}.$$

A linear combination of products $p_I(T)p_J(T)$ that vanishes on all Boolean diagonal matrices is a sum of terms of the form $$\label{eq:slack-coefficient-patterns}
 cMN\,T_{ij},\qquad
 cMN\,T_{ij}(T_{ii}-1),\qquad
 cMN\,(T_{ii}^2-T_{ii}),$$ where $i\ne j$ in the first two forms, $c\in\mathbb F$, and $M,N$ are arbitrary square minors of $T$, possibly empty.

Put $\gamma=10^{-3}$. Suppose the line law of a function $P:G\to\mathbb F$ fails with probability at most $\delta^2$, where $\delta>0$ satisfies $$\begin{aligned}
 2\delta+\lambda_1&<\gamma/2,\notag\\
 1-4\gamma-4\delta-2/(q-1)&>\delta+\lambda_1,\label{eq:correction-smallness}\\
 27\gamma+5\delta&<1.\notag
\end{aligned}$$ There is a scalar-invariant set $H$ of directions of $\mathsf D$-mass at least $1-\delta$, and a function $P'$ differing from $P$ on at most $2\delta$ of $G$, such that $t\mapsto P'(A+th)$ has degree at most two for every $A$ and $h\in H$.

Suppose a scalar-invariant set of directions has $\mathsf D$-mass at least $1-\rho$, and $F:G\to\mathbb F$ has degree at most $D<q-1$ on every line in those directions. Then either $F=0$ identically or $$\mu(\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}F)\geq 1-\rho-\frac{D}{q-1}-\lambda_1.$$

There is a fixed finite family of primitive types $(P_s,p_s)$ and ordered comparisons, and a fixed $\zeta>0$, constructible in polynomial time from the input formula, with the following properties.*

1.  *Each predicate depends on boundedly many bit positions. All samplers are polynomially enumerable finite rational laws with inverse-polynomial positive seed probabilities.*

2.  *Constant-one and constant-zero types are included, with calibrations one and zero. Every comparison marginal is a primitive type, and every type has a comparison to the constant-one type.*

3.  *In a satisfiable instance, evaluation at the perfect assignment $y^*$ satisfies $\mathbb E_{P_s}R(y^*)=p_s$ for every type.*

4.  *In an unsatisfiable instance, no Boolean valuation is $\zeta$-calibrated and ordered.*

*The numbers $p_s$, the number of types and comparisons, and $\zeta$ are independent of the input size.

Fix the numerical type data, the comparison-type pairs, positive constants $b_0,K_0,B_0$, and a tolerance $\zeta>0$. There is an integer $t_0$ such that, for every $t\ge t_0$, there is $\varepsilon_0(t)>0$ with the following property. Set $p=p_*^t$ and take $0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_0(t)$. Suppose that $0W(r')\bigr)&\le\varepsilon v \quad\text{for every lifted comparison.} \label{eq:entropy-lifted-order} \end{aligned}$$ Then there exists a single Boolean valuation $H$ satisfying Equation [eq:entropy-valuation-target].* *The choices of $t_0$ and $\varepsilon_0(t)$ depend only on $b_0,K_0,B_0,\zeta$, the finite type and comparison lists, and $(\omega_s,p_s)_{s\in\mathcal T}$. They are uniform in $\mathcal X$, the primitive supports, their atom probabilities, and the particular comparison couplings with the prescribed marginals. Types with $p_s=0$ are allowed.

For each fixed $T_0\ge1$, the primitive system of Section 4 admits a demand law $\mu$ of scores and a finite sum $\mathcal D$ of raw comparison forms with the following properties. All arities, score bounds, numerical dimensions, and total comparison weight are bounded by constants independent of the input size. The laws and weights do not depend on a lookup. At a perfect witness $x$, $$\int|B(x)-B'(x)|\,\mathrm d\mathfrak m(B,B')\le4, \qquad \mu\{B:B(x)\ge1/4\},\ \mu\{B:B(x)\le-1/4\}\ge10^{-4}.$$ In a NO instance, every binary measurable lookup with $\nu=\mathop{\mathrm{Var}}_\mu(h)>0$ satisfies $\mathcal D(h)>T_0\nu$. Conditional on the discrete sampling data, the numerical laws and score entries belong to fixed finite families of polynomials with rational coefficients on rational boxes, with atoms represented as separate cases.

Choose $k=\lceil\rho^{-1}\rceil$ and require $n_j\ge4k$. With $c=4^{-(k+2)}$, Equation [eq:resampling-bound] implies $$\label{eq:amplitude-signal} \|b^0\|_\Sigma^2\le\nu,\qquad \sum_j s_j^2\sum_{i\in I_j}\mathbb E[|b_i^0|^2\mid\mathcal B]\le\tfrac14, \qquad \|g^0\|_\Sigma^2\ge c\nu.$$ The constants $k,c$ depend only on $T_0$.

The demand law and the raw comparison measures in Theorem 13 have polynomially enumerable discrete seeds, whose positive probabilities are bounded below by an inverse polynomial in input size. For each seed, after finitely many fixed subdivisions of numerical boxes, their conditional densities are nonnegative rational polynomials and the score table entries are rational polynomials of bounded degree in a fixed number of numerical variables. There are only finitely many such numerical polynomial patterns, independent of input size. The total raw comparison mass is finite and bounded by a constant. For any fixed finite grid and deterministic entrywise rounding rule, every positive rounded demand mass or comparison-pair mass has an inverse-polynomial lower bound.
